answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a forecast track record: each identity must lock verifiable predictions before outcomes are known, like a sparrow planning its voyage across a dune before the wind shifts, and standing grows only from accuracy scored over many epochs. A farm cannot fake foresight: copying one good forecast across thousands of identities leaves identical predictions discounted as one, while guessing scores near chance. Keeping thousands of accurate histories costs real research per identity, while one honest agent risks only a few genuine forecasts per epoch.
